question: What is the primary role of communication in community health nursing?

options.A: Building therapeutic relationships and driving behavioral change
options.D: Enforcing hospital policies in rural clinics

explanation: Communication is the core tool nurses use to connect with patients and encourage positive health choices. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h1)

question: Why does community health communication differ from acute care hospital communication?

options.A: Community settings require less attention to cultural factors than hospitals
options.B: Hospital settings rely entirely on non-verbal cues rather than spoken words
options.C: Community settings involve engaging people in their natural environments with diverse social dynamics
options.D: Hospital settings focus exclusively on long-term preventive education

explanation: Community nursing takes place outside controlled hospital walls, requiring nurses to adapt to homes, markets, and varying social structures. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h1)

question: What component of the communication process represents the response from the receiver?
explanation: Feedback allows the sender to know if the message was received and correctly understood by the listener. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: A nurse uses a pictorial chart to explain immunization schedules to a mother. What does the chart represent in the communication process?
explanation: The medium or method used to transmit the message, such as a visual chart or spoken word, is the communication channel. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: Which action is an example of effective verbal communication in patient care?

options.A: Speaking as quickly as possible to save clinical time
options.B: Using complex clinical jargon to show professional expertise
options.C: Avoiding direct questions about the patient's symptoms
options.D: Translating medical terms into simple, relatable language

explanation: Simple language ensures the patient truly comprehends their health status without feeling intimidated. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h3)

question: Why must a community health nurse be mindful of non-verbal cues regarding eye contact?

options.A: Patients always prefer intense, unbroken eye contact during assessments
options.B: Eye contact has no impact on how patients perceive healthcare providers
options.C: Cultural norms dictate whether direct eye contact is viewed as polite or disrespectful
options.D: Direct eye contact prevents the transmission of infectious airborne diseases

explanation: Non-verbal behaviors carry different meanings across cultures, and misinterpreting them can damage rapport. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h3)

question: What is the key difference between hearing and active listening?

options.A: Hearing requires conscious mental effort while listening is automatic
options.B: Active listening is a deliberate, focused clinical skill requiring full attention
options.C: Hearing only occurs in clinical settings unlike active listening
options.D: Active listening involves ignoring non-verbal emotional cues

explanation: Active listening requires concentration, reflection, and engagement, going beyond mere passive sound perception. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: How does demonstrating empathy impact the nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: It speeds up the physical examination process significantly
options.B: It validates the patient's emotional experience and builds deep trust
options.C: It encourages the patient to rely solely on family members for advice
options.D: It causes the nurse to lose professional objectivity completely

explanation: Empathy makes patients feel seen and understood, which fosters openness and cooperation in their care plan. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common category of communication barriers?
explanation: Mathematical barriers are not a recognized category of interpersonal communication obstruction in nursing. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h5)

question: A nurse is trying to conduct a health talk in a bustling local market, but the surrounding noise drowns out her voice. What type of barrier is primarily affecting this interaction?
explanation: Environmental noise and poor physical surroundings fall under physical barriers to communication. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h5)

question: What is the foundational starting point for developing cultural competence?

options.A: Speaking at least three major international languages
options.B: Self-awareness of one's own personal biases and values
options.C: Memorizing every ethnic group's traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Strictly prohibiting the use of home remedies in all cases

explanation: Culturally competent care starts when nurses recognize how their own background influences their perceptions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h6)

question: How should a community nurse respond when a client mentions using traditional remedies alongside prescribed medications?

options.A: Ignore the comment and pretend traditional remedies do not exist
options.B: Insist that the client stop all modern medication immediately
options.C: Threaten to report the client to local law enforcement authorities
options.D: Explore the practices respectfully and negotiate a safe treatment plan

explanation: Respectful dialogue bridges the gap between traditional practices and modern healthcare without alienating the patient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h6)

question: Which technique is most appropriate when communicating with an older adult experiencing hearing loss?

options.A: Facing the client directly and speaking in a moderate, clear tone
options.B: Shouting loudly directly into the patient's ear from behind
options.C: Directing all educational information exclusively to family members
options.D: Writing all instructions down without speaking a single word

explanation: Facing the client allows them to read lips and observe facial expressions, which aids comprehension alongside moderate volume. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h7)

question: Why is kneeling to eye level an effective communication strategy when interacting with young children?

options.A: It is required by standard pediatric hospital protocols
options.B: It prevents children from running away during the health talk
options.C: It reduces intimidation and creates a less threatening environment
options.D: It makes physical examinations go twice as fast

explanation: Standing tall over a child increases fear and power imbalances; lowering oneself promotes psychological safety. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of using the teach-back method during health education?

options.A: To verify patient comprehension by having them repeat instructions in their own words
options.B: To fulfill mandatory legal documentation requirements
options.C: To evaluate how well the nurse delivered the lecture
options.D: To test the client's memory capacity for clinical statistics

explanation: Teach-back ensures that the patient understood the guidance correctly rather than just nodding politely. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h8)

question: What standard should guide a nurse when writing clinical notes in a patient record?

options.A: Notes should include personal opinions about the patient's attitude
options.B: Notes can be delayed for several days if the clinic is busy
options.C: Notes should be objective, legible, and record actual observations without personal bias
options.D: Notes should use informal abbreviations and local slang to save space

explanation: Objective documentation ensures legal safety and accurate continuity of care among multidisciplinary team members. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h8)
